newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister calls for global human cloning ban.
newsitem.headline: German minister calls for global human cloning ban.

text.p: German Research Minister Juergen Ruettgers on Wednesday called for a worldwide ban on cloning human beings and denounced pro-cloning arguments used by some scientists that he said mirrored the Nazis' way of thinking.

Ruettgers said cloning was already outlawed in Germany and he hoped a similar worldwide ban on human embryo research could be adopted by the United Nations Education Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO).
"I believe that, within the framework of UNESCO, we need to ensure that cloning is banned worldwide," Ruettgers told Deutschland radio.
"We simply cannot stand by and allow humans to be copied. That would be breaking through an ethical barrier that goes far beyond even the barrier of the atomic bomb."
News that scientists have cloned sheep has stirred painful memories in Germany of Nazi attempts to breed a "master race" of blue-eyed and blond-haired Aryans.

"The door has been opened for turning humans into instruments," said Karlheinz Steinmueller, a German scientist, in an interview with SAT1 television. "Advertisers may one day be able to offer you babies with blue eyes and blond hair."

Reflecting its shame over horrific Nazi experiments on humans, Germany has strict limits on genetic research and the public is fiercely opposed to genetic manipulation even of simple agricultural products. Surrogate motherhood is outlawed.

Evelyne Gebhardt, a European member of parliament, said she would urge the European Commission to quickly start work on a directive that would make it a crime throughout the EU to tamper with the human embryo.
"The EU needs standarised protection against the possibility of a biotech derailment," Gebhardt said in a statement.
Ruettgers said it was "perverse" for scientists in the United States to defend the possibility of cloning humans for medical reasons, such as making it easier to transplant organs.

"That shows how perverse this process would be," Ruettgers said. "Humans would be then bred for spare parts and then later carved up. That is the exactly the same thinking that drove the Nazis to their research on human breeding."

U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday banned federally-funded human cloning and asked private scientists voluntarily to enact a similar moratorium while government advisers review the ethically troublesome issue.
The prospect of human cloning hit the headlines last month week scientists in Scotland introduced the world to Dolly, a lamb cloned from an adult sheep.
The subject has touched a raw nerve in Germany.
The cover of the latest issue of news magazine Der Spiegel features a line of Adolf Hitlers marching next to columns of Albert Einsteins and Claudia Schiffers.
Standing next to the clones of Hitler is Dolly the sheep.
"Science on the way to cloning humans" reads the cover story heading, which leads a 10-page story on the subject.
